chapter: Part Two: theaters and the Chicago scene
title: After-hours spots and jam sessions
summary: Describes places at 55th, the Panama, and the Three Deuces.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Right. Well, did the guys hang out a lot together, or was everybody working so much you didn't get to see each other very often?
We used to hang out in different after-hour joints.
What were some of those?
Well, there was one at 55th, under the el there, 55th Place, where we used to get together. Earl and Art Tatum used to hook up, and jam sessions when we'd get off.
Were there -- you know, New York, there was an awful lot of what they'd call cutting contests.
Yeah.
Guys would come into town, and they'd have to fight their way --
Well, it was the same thing. They called it jam sessions here, but it was the same thing.
Uh-huh. Guys come in from out of town, and they'd have to sort of prove themselves --
Prove themselves, that's right.
Do you remember any particular ones?
I never sat in any in New York.
I mean in Chicago?

Chicago? Well, I sat in on a few of them. I can't remember. All I can remember is you used to go around to after hours spots and hang out. And sometimes you'd have a jam session when the guys would get off. They'd come by there and the Panama on 58th Street was one of them. Where Nat King Cole got started.
The Three Deuces downtown was well known.
We had -- Roy Eldridge was down there.
But even before --
We had a lot of jam sessions down there before Roy, yeah.
Do you know Eddie Fritz, piano player?
Yeah.

Eddie was telling me that he remembers a session down there when Louie was still in town. And Louie was there, and Baby Dodds, and didn't have a piano player, the piano player didn't show up, so he played with them. Said it was, you know, a regular thing. Guys would drop in, and jam. Must have been --
That might have been before my time, when Louie was here.
Sounds like a very exciting time to be a musician, and --
Yeah.
-- Chicago, play all day and all night.
All day and all night. I got in on the middle of it.
Yeah.
In the middle twenties.
